3.3.4.1-f18.text: Ne se Cadurcis destitutam fasciis, / Nudam Caleno concumbentem videat.

translations.literal: Lest he see her(self), deprived of the Cadurcan bands, / naked, lying with Calenus.
translations.note: Burton's syntax ('ne se … videat') is awkward and the sense is partly a guess. The Cadurci were a Gallic people known for linen; 'fasciae' are the girths or webbing of a bed. The lines are by the Roman poetess Sulpicia, wife of Calenus. The text preserved by the scholiast reads roughly 'si me cadurci restitutis fasciis / nudam Caleno concubantem proferat' ('if, with the bed-girths restored, it should show me lying naked with Calenus'). Burton's 'ne se … destitutam … videat' differs and changes the sense.
